results.summary: The QTCore-A1 is an accumulator-based 8-bit microarchitecture with a Von Neumann design, featuring 19 registers for memory and I/O. It is programmed and controlled via an SPI interface using a scan chain that allows reading and writing all internal registers. Testing requires an external microcontroller with an SPI peripheral to load programs and provide a clock. Notably, the entire functional Verilog was generated through conversations with GPT-4, making it an experiment in AI-assisted hardware design.

spiPWMio provides a PWM generator on output pin 7 and a PWM reader on input pin 7, with the generator's duty cycle set by input pins and the reader's value reflected on output pins. When the SPI interface is used, the module's behavior can be reconfigured. Testing can be done by looping the PWM output back to the input and verifying the configuration on the outputs. The design can be tested with a development kit and optionally an oscilloscope or signal generator.

ChipTune is an 8-bit Programmable Sound Generator that replicates the Audio Processing Unit of vintage video games, producing square, triangle, and noise waveforms. It receives commands via a UART serial interface at 9600 baud and outputs PWM audio. Testing requires a computer COM port and an analog PWM filter with an audio driver. The design includes four independent sound channels and is controlled by writing to internal registers through the serial link.

This project implements an 8-bit signed Baugh-Wooley multiplier that computes the product of two 8-bit two's complement numbers in a single clock cycle. The operands are applied to the input pins, and the 16-bit result is split across the output pins. Testing involves applying values and reading the result after one clock cycle. The design was developed as part of a neural network project and adapted for the restricted I/O of Tiny Tapeout.

This design implements a 60 Hz grid-forming reference and linear dump-load controller for driving micro-inverters, using a CORDIC block to generate a sine wave. It produces bipolar PWM signals for an H-bridge and controls a dump load based on sampled AC and DC voltages. Testing requires a real or modeled grid-tied solar system, including an H-bridge, transformer, and ADC with isolated instrumentation. The design is intended for industrial power applications and includes protection features for over- and under-voltage conditions.

Solo Squash is a VGA game that displays a bouncing ball in a playfield with three walls and a player-controlled paddle, using a 25 MHz clock for 640x480 resolution. The player uses up/down buttons to move the paddle, and the game produces tones on a speaker for bounces. Testing requires resistors to connect the VGA outputs to a monitor, buttons for input, and optionally an amplifier for sound. The design also includes a leading zero counter experiment that outputs the count on the bidirectional pins.

This is a simple 4-bit current output DAC that sinks a current proportional to the 4-bit digital input applied to the digital pins. Testing involves applying a 4-bit signal and measuring the output current on the analog pin with a resistive load. The design is purely analog and occupies 1x2 tiles. No further documentation is provided beyond the basic description.

This project implements a stepper motor controller using a Moore state machine that supports full-step, half-step, and double-step modes, with selectable speeds of 1s, 0.5s, 0.25s, and 0.125s. The direction (clockwise or counterclockwise) and step type are controlled by input pins. Testing was performed on an FPGA with a 50 MHz clock, and the design outputs four coil drive signals. The project is educational and demonstrates state machine design for motor control.

This project implements a set of AND gates that combine the eight input bits to produce four output bits, intended as an introduction to Tiny Tapeout. The documentation states the author is still figuring out how it works. Testing is described as flipping dip switches, and external hardware includes a 7-segment display. The design is minimal and serves as a learning exercise.

This project is a preliminary test of the Tiny Tapeout method and system, with no functional description provided. The documentation states it is currently just a test and has no defined behavior. No external hardware is listed. The design is essentially empty and serves only as a placeholder.
